chunks: Muḥammad ibn Muslim asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and said to him:
A man intends to travel; when does he shorten? He said: “When he is concealed from the houses.”
He said: I said to him, a man intends to travel and leaves when the sun declines, so he said: “When you leave, then perform salat of two rakʿahs.”

key_terms.السَّفَرَ: travel or journey that affects the ruling of salat
key_terms.الْبُيُوتِ: the houses of the town, marking the boundary for travel rulings
key_terms.تَزُولُ: to decline, referring to the sun passing midday
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ: two rakʿahs, the shortened form of the prayer

ai.seo_question: When does a traveler begin shortening salat according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on salat during travel. It states that the traveler begins to shorten salat once he is no longer visible among the houses, and if he departs at midday, he is to perform salat as two rakʿahs upon leaving.
